label: input token w at position 0 or 1 of the original sequence
explanation: Fires only when the input token is w during the first two original-input steps (t=0 or t=1). Every such step activates (precision 1.0), at near-saturated magnitude (median 1.396, max 1.40), split roughly evenly between t=0 and t=1. The only misses are w at t=2, which fire very weakly (about 0.04 of max, 0.1% of activation mass). Silent on w at t>=3, on every other token, on the delimiter, and during the copy phase (just one copy-phase activation in the dev split). Magnitude is essentially flat; sequence length and the surrounding tokens hardly matter. The few low-quartile cases (about 0.87-0.9 of max) are w at t=1.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split there are 0 false positives (precision 1.0) and 335 misses holding about 0.05% of activation mass. All of the misses are w at t=2 with activations of 0.03-0.09 of max, which matches what the explanation says.

Factual claims check out on dev. All activation mass falls in the original-input phase, the delimiter has 0 activations, and the copy phase has exactly 1 stray activation (at t=16). Activations split 52% at t=0 and 48% at t=1. The feature fires only on in_tok w, with mean 1.335, median 1.396 and max 1.40.
The low-magnitude claim is confirmed. The predicate (in_tok==w)&(t==1) covers 96% of the bottom two activation quartiles and 0-7% of the top two, so the weaker cases are indeed w at t=1.
The widened predicate t<=2 does worse: precision drops to 0.68 and F1 to 0.81, because w at t=2 mostly does not fire. The original predicate is the better one.
Minor point: by_to_go and by_L show only that w at t<=1 makes up a larger share of steps in short sequences. This does not count against the 'little effect of length' claim.
